## Summary

A September 2 recorded conversation with George Noble, published September 21, connects AI funding risk, heavy debt issuance, Japanese capital flows and narrative-driven valuations. Eisman stresses borrower profitability and customer concentration; Noble supplies the strongest AI-collapse and Tesla/SpaceX short claims. The review preserves Eisman's explicit statement that Noble may be more bearish than he is.

Empirical premises and forecasts are assessed separately. Guest assertions are not Eisman forecasts. Unverified magnitudes and causal attribution remain unresolved.

<a id="substack-215442435-c026"></a>
### 026. A debt-to-GDP comparison suggests Japanese ten-year yields should be near 7%, versus about 4% observed; domestic ownership reduces the effective debt burden.

**Mixed** | George Noble | explanation | major

[Source at 24:13-25:36](https://realeismanplaybook.substack.com/p/stock-picking-in-difficult-times) | Stance: asserted | Horizon: not stated

The chart and quoted yield levels are unverified. Gross debt, net debt and domestic ownership are distinct concepts; resident ownership alone does not subtract the government's liability. Debt ratios alone also do not identify a fair nominal yield.

Conditional reasoning: Changing a bondholder from foreign to domestic changes ownership but leaves the government liability unchanged. Domestic ownership can affect funding stability, not mechanically convert gross debt into net debt.

Assessment test: Inspect the relevant original financial, operational or economic data and compare the claimed mechanism with competing explanations.

Further verification: Recheck the original data and subsequent realized outcomes.

It does not announce a new Treasury currency swap or a loan to buy JGBs.
- [FIMA Repo Facility FAQs](https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fima-repo-facility-faqs.htm) (updated 2024-02-21): FIMA is a Federal Reserve repo facility allowing eligible foreign monetary authorities to obtain temporary dollars against Treasury collateral, avoiding outright Treasury sales. It is distinct from a currency swap and does not itself require JGB purchases.

## Framework and tools

- Trace supplier revenue to end-user economics and financing sources.
- Circular financing is a warning signal, not automatic default.
- Account for macro factors and currency exposure in stock selection.
- Separate long-run investment value from daily price moves and technology usefulness.
- Distinguish receivables concentration from revenue concentration.

Tools and charts discussed, not a complete visual inspection:

- NVIDIA Q2 FY2027 receivables concentration.
- Debt-to-GDP versus yield chart is described but not reconstructed.
- Unhedged yen return arithmetic.
- Tesla Q3 financial summary and operating/FCF distinctions.
- FIMA repo mechanics compared with the guest's swap-line account.

## Source cautions

Steve Eisman hosts George Noble. SPEAKER_00 generally denotes Eisman and SPEAKER_01 Noble, but speaker markers contain obvious turn-boundary errors. Guest short targets remain guest claims; the host's closing summary is not a wholesale endorsement.
- All 1,201 normalized transcript segments were read in full.
- Noble explicitly dates the recording September 2, 2026 at about 1938 seconds; publication is September 21.
- Publisher speaker markers sometimes assign both sides of an exchange to one label. Attribution follows question-and-answer context; short confirmations are not separate predictions.
- Eisman's 40-basis-point AI rate effect is explicitly an invented illustrative number.
- Tesla PDF financial table was inspected via primary-source search extraction; PDF screenshot output was not usable, and no claim of a complete PDF read is made.
- No verified short-entry records or total trading returns were available.
